Re: Search Atlas - contract role

You said: "Looking for 3+ years PM in B2B SaaS with an actual technical background"

Here is how I would approach it.

I would build the integration with the failure cases handled first - retries, rate limits, and a clear alert when an upstream source is down rather than silent bad data. Credentials stay in environment secrets. Tests cover the parsing so a provider format change is caught.

What you would get:
  - The completed work product in the format you specified
  - The script or process used, so you can re-run it yourself
  - A short note on method and any data-quality issues found

Availability: I can start within a week and commit consistent hours; happy to begin with a small scoped piece so you can see how I work before committing to more.

Relevant work I have actually built and run:
- Odds, schedule, roster, injury, weather and news providers, each with credential-state degradation.
- ruff + mypy + pytest + secret scanning + dependency audit in CI, and verify-before-publish that refuses to deploy a broken dashboard build.

These are my own production systems, not client references, and I am happy to walk you through the code and the deployment.

One question before I start: What should happen when the upstream API rate-limits us mid-run - back off and resume, or fail the run loudly?

For transparency: I use AI tooling as part of my workflow, under my own review. Every deliverable is checked against your acceptance criteria before it reaches you. If you would prefer this work done without AI assistance, tell me and I will price it that way.

Andres Mercado

prop_e3c83c659f00.body:
Re: [DEMO] Clean and consolidate 14 monthly sales spreadsheets into one reporting workbook

You said: "We have 14 monthly Excel exports from our POS system, one per month, each with slightly different column names and some merged header rows"

Here is how I would approach it.

I would write a repeatable script rather than doing this once by hand, so you can re-run it yourself next period. The script normalizes the differing headers to one schema, preserves every source row (rows that fail to map get flagged, never dropped), and outputs the consolidated workbook plus a mapping note. I verify by comparing row counts, column counts and totals before and after - if the numbers do not reconcile, it is not done.

What you would get:
  - Preserve every original row (we will check row counts)
  - Flag any rows that failed to map rather than dropping them
  - And keep currency formatting consistent

Timeline: 4-5 business days from a confirmed brief.

Relevant work I have actually built and run:
- Two production pipelines (NFL, MLB) ingesting multiple third-party data sources on a schedule.
- Static dashboards built by CI and published to GitHub Pages, mobile-responsive with offline support.

These are my own production systems, not client references, and I am happy to walk you through the code and the deployment.

One question before I start: When two source files disagree on the same record, which one should win - the newer file, or a specific source of truth?

For transparency: I use AI tooling as part of my workflow, under my own review. Every deliverable is checked against your acceptance criteria before it reaches you. If you would prefer this work done without AI assistance, tell me and I will price it that way.

Andres Mercado
